opening: Lord, meet us gently today and always
body:
It began with almost nothing—five barley loaves and two fish. Not abundance. Not enough. Just what was offered. Placed into the hands of Christ, it was blessed, broken, and given away.  And somehow, in the giving, it multiplied.  The crowd did not leave hungry.  They ate until they were satisfied—fully, completely filled. No one rationing, no one overlooked. Then Christ did something unexpected. He did not dismiss the leftovers or allow them to remain in the dirt.  He gave a command:

“Gather the fragments left over, so that nothing will be wasted.”

So the apostles went back. Step by step, through the same crowd that had just been fed, they bent down and picked up what seemed like crumbs— small, broken pieces of what had already been used. It took time. But they gathered anyway. And when they finished, what looked like fragments had become fullness again. Twelve baskets. More after the breaking than before the beginning.

In our lives, we look at what we didn’t do, what fell apart, what we didn’t complete— and we call it waste.

But Christ does not. He says, " Gather it.

The unfinished moments.
The days that slipped past.
The efforts that felt too small to count.
The whatever fits here for you......

They may feel like crumbs in your hands— insignificant, broken, not enough to matter. But gathered, they become something else. Not wasted effort. Not failure.

Bread.

Because nothing placed in His hands—and nothing gathered in obedience—
is ever lost.
